body: I wasn't able to reproduce this with ELSER, but ELSER is a special case for memory calculations so maybe it is different. I'll try again with a different model

this doesn't seem to be the case for the reranker model either, although I see it is reporting `per_deployment_memory_bytes": 0, "per_allocation_memory_bytes": 0`, so maybe that explains it. I'll try uploading a model with eland to see what happens

I was able to reproduce this error when the model was installed with eland 

```
first deployment:
                "required_native_memory_bytes": 992216732
second deployment:
                "required_native_memory_bytes": 1332104964
update deployment:
                "required_native_memory_bytes": 2351769660
```

Looking into the code more, I think that this is actually how this code was intended to function, and we can't simply change it without it becoming confusing. 

For example, here is the stats potput for a model uploaded with eland:

We can see that the `required_native_memory_bytes` field is under `model_size_stats`, rather than `deployment_stats`. This distinction is reflected in the code, and is the reason that the memory requirements for all allocations in a model are combined. 

We could change the meaning of this field, and change the value, but that would require some refactoring, and would likely constitute a breaking change. 

If there is a reason that we want each deployment to have its memory requirements listed separately, we should probably add that to the `deployment_stats` section rather than changing `model_size_stats`.

Given the above, I would suggest we close this issue as "non-issue"/won't change.

issue.title: [ML] Model allocator attempts to locate model on nodes with insufficient memory

labels.name: Team:ML
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
When attempting to start a model, it fails because the attempt is being made on a node that does not have sufficient memory.

In one instance a user had 2x 16 gb ML nodes. One node had nearly all it's memory consumed and another node had no models deployed to it. ML attempt to deploy the model on the node that had very little memory left instead of locating the deployment on the ML node with sufficient memory.

body: If we implement https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/139233, we would be able to report the actual memory usage of the deployment process instead of the estimated one.
